title: Optimizing dev-to-prod workflow for processing 38M+ rows with DuckDB and Polars on AWS Graviton3
body: I am developing a Python data pipeline to process and enrich the Brazilian Federal Revenue (CNPJ) dataset, which consists of monthly sharded CSV files totaling over 38 million rows (approx. 100GB+ raw). Current Stack: Engine: Hybrid use of Polars (for complex regex filtering on secondary activities) and DuckDB (for SQL-native unions and joins with geographic reference tables). Storage: Final output in compressed Parquet . Infrastructure: Local development with 8GB RAM for testing samples, followed by deployment to AWS EC2 r7g.xlarge (Graviton3) instances for full runs. Current Workflow: Extract a small sample locally. Validate transformation logic and regex filters. Manually deploy the script to AWS and run against the full 12-month dataset. The Challenge: The "sample locally -> deploy to cloud" cycle feels slow. While my local tests pass, the full-scale run sometimes encounters memory pressure or I/O bottlenecks when spilling to disk on AWS. I am looking for ways to improve productivity and maintain low costs. Questions: Is there a better way to simulate "cloud-scale" memory constraints locally without manual sampling? How can I further optimize DuckDB’s TEMP_DIRECTORY on local NVMe vs. EBS to ensure that a 38M row join doesn't stall the CPU?
